To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the GC content of the transcript is not a significant factor in the expression levels in C. reinhardtiii; (2) the codon usage is important for expression levels; (3) the presence of splicing signals in the coding region has a significant effect on gene expression; (4) the folding energy in the 5’ UTR has a significant effect of gene expression.
the GC content, the presence of splice sites and the folding energy around the start codon are the most influential features that affect gene expression in C. reinhardtiii.
the GC-content and mRNA folding energy in a window of 200 nucleotides around translation initiation affect the expression of a heterologous gene in the model microalgae Chlamydomonias reinhardtii.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of heterologous gene sequences for use in the microalgae C. reinhardtiii, which can lead to improved expression levels of heterologous genes.

the identification of sequence features that can enhance heterologous expression, and with the development of a novel computational method that can be used to predict the optimal sequence for a desired target protein.
the optimization of heterologous gene sequences, and the identification of key features in the C. reinhardtii transcript that affect gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most optimal sequence for expression in C. reinhardtiii is one that is highly expressed in the native organism and is highly similar to the natural transcript sequence, while maintaining a GC content similar to the native transcript.
the most significant feature of the synthetic transcript that affects expression level is the codon bias, followed by the splicing signal and the folding energy.
a combination of all three factors is essential for optimal gene expression in C. reinhardtiii.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gene expression in C. reinhardtiii can be enhanced by optimizing transcript sequences.
the combination of computational and empirical methods enables us to understand the way in which gene expression is encoded within the C. reinhardi transcripts.
the combination of in silico and in vivo methods can provide insights into the way gene expression works in microalgae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sequence optimization can be utilized to improve heterologous expression of nuclear genes in C. reinhardtiii.

the combination of computational analysis and empirical measurements can be used to understand the way gene expression levels are encoded in transcripts, and can be used to improve gene expression in microalgal cells.
by using computational tools, we were able to identify the key factors that affect heterologous protein expression in microalgas and that these factors differ significantly from other organisms.
